field_name: Context construction and supervision for multi-hop knowledge-graph question answering

categories.name: Inference-time context construction (retrieval, prompting, agents)
categories.description: Methods that leave the reader language model frozen and improve multi-hop KGQA by choosing which KG triples to place in the prompt/context at inference.

categories.name: Subgraph retrieval with merging and ordering
categories.description: Retrieve a local subgraph with Cypher/SPARQL, deduplicate/merge overlapping triplets, and impose an order before prompting.

categories.name: Learned/agentic context engineering under resource budgets
categories.description: Treat context construction as a sequential decision process and learn the selection policy (e.g., constrained multi-agent RL) with latency/token budgets.

categories.name: Controlled prompt-composition ablation
categories.description: Systematically vary which triples, syntax, order, and grounding instruction enter the prompt, using gold subgraphs to remove retriever variance.

categories.name: Training-free graph-text memory co-evolution
categories.description: Maintain synchronized textual and relational working memory during reasoning, extracting triples from text and injecting graph facts back into generation.

categories.name: Knowledge-augmented language model architectures
categories.description: Methods that change the model architecture or input representation to fuse a KG subgraph with language, trained on downstream QA labels.

categories.name: Subgraph reasoning modules fused with pretrained language models
categories.description: Multi-hop graph relation networks over extracted KG subgraphs, unifying path-based reasoning and GNNs.

categories.name: Latent-path / variational training from QA pairs
categories.description: Learn multi-hop reasoning from question-answer pairs alone with latent variables, without explicit reasoning-chain supervision.

categories.name: Sparse-KG prompting with link extrapolation
categories.description: Prompt the LLM to build entity groups and probe plausible (factual and extrapolated) relationships to compensate for very sparse KGs.

categories.name: KG-embedding-based multi-hop KGQA
categories.description: Use knowledge graph embeddings and missing-link prediction so multi-hop QA can be answered over sparse KGs without restricting answers to a prespecified neighborhood.

categories.name: Reinforcement-learning-based training for structured/graph reasoning
categories.description: Train models (or policies) with RL to perform graph-structured reasoning, query parsing, or context selection.

categories.name: RL over executable query formalisms (SQL/Cypher)
categories.description: Joint RL + CoT over relational and graph query languages with topology-aware rewards, inducing cross-formalism transfer and zero-shot downstream QA gains.

categories.name: RL over context-selection policies
categories.description: Constrained multi-agent RL that learns what to expand and keep in the prompt under resource budgets.

categories.name: Training-time supervision-signal design for KG reasoning
categories.description: The category the proposed idea occupies: changing what the model is trained on (triple/path supervision, context-enriched supervision, corrective examples) rather than only what it sees at inference.

categories.name: Knowledge-in-context for knowledge graph completion
categories.parent: Training-time supervision-signal design for KG reasoning
categories.description: Give an LLM additional KG facts in context to predict missing head-relation-tail links (link prediction, not multi-hop QA).

categories.name: Proposed: same-passage context-enriched triple/path supervision + adaptive repair loop + low-hop RL
categories.parent: Training-time supervision-signal design for KG reasoning
categories.description: Fine-tune with a local context subgraph drawn from the same source passage as the target triple/path, compare triple-only vs context-enriched regimes, repair one-hop failures with generated corrective examples, then apply RL on lower-hop instances and test transfer to deeper hops.

idea_position: The idea sits in the 'Training-time supervision-signal design for KG reasoning' category, and specifically in an empty sub-category (same-passage context-enriched triple/path supervision + repair loop + low-hop RL). Every analyzed high-relevance work instead occupies the 'Inference-time context construction' category (SG-RAG MOT, CLAUSE, the answer-path prompt study, Co-E) or the 'Knowledge-augmented LM architectures' / 'KG-embedding' categories. The closest neighbors are inference-time subgraph curation (A1-A3) and RL policy training (C2); no analyzed paper changes the fine-tuning supervision signal by adding same-passage context triples, and none reports hop-depth transfer from shallow-only training.
dominant_approaches: Retrieve/assemble a local KG subgraph and prompt a frozen or lightly adapted LLM (SG-RAG MOT, CLAUSE, Co-E, answer-path study)
Fuse a KG subgraph with a pretrained language model through a dedicated graph module (GreaseLM/MHGRN)
Use KG embeddings and missing-link prediction to cope with sparsity (EmbedKGQA)
Learn context selection or query parsing with RL under rewards/budgets (CLAUSE, STRuCT-LLM)
Training-free prompting that builds or extrapolates a relational context around the query (GIVE, Co-E)
common_assumptions: A bounded local subgraph of triples is the right evidence container for multi-hop questions.
Adding relevant KG triples to the model's context improves multi-hop accuracy (explicitly challenged by the answer-path study and by CLAUSE's over-retrieval finding).
The reader model or its training supervision need not change; most methods operate on context at inference.
Reasoning paths / gold subgraphs are obtainable (gold SPARQL, path supervision) and can be used for training or evaluation.
Hop depth (chain length) is the primary difficulty axis of multi-hop QA.
KG incompleteness and noise are handled by retrieval, extrapolation, or embeddings rather than by repairing the training supervision.
Answer accuracy on standard benchmarks (MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ/CommonsenseQA) is the primary success criterion, sometimes with latency/token budgets.
common_benchmarks: Knowledge graph completion (standard KGC benchmarks, names not retrieved for KICGPT)

repeated_limitations.description: Context is constructed or curated at inference; the language model's training supervision is not the manipulated variable, so it is untested whether a better training signal (not better retrieval) is what multi-hop KGQA needs.
No per-hop-depth breakdown or explicit shallow-to-deep transfer measurement; results are reported at aggregate or single-depth level (e.g., MetaQA-2-hop headline, zero-shot KGQA gain only +1.7%).
Base facts are trusted as-is: sparsity/noise is compensated by extrapolation, retrieval, or link prediction, and errors are not detected and repaired in a training loop.
Evaluation is often on a single benchmark or narrow domain (e.g., MetaQA only; UMLS/ConceptNet; CommonsenseQA/OpenbookQA), limiting generality of the claims.
Inaccessible or missing evidence (no abstract/full text) prevents verification of method and result overlap for some works.

Training-based approaches either use large models/heavy RL infrastructure or use latent variables rather than explicit context supervision, making them hard to compare against lightweight context-enriched fine-tuning.

underexplored_combinations: Training-time context-enriched supervision for multi-hop KGQA under a matched supervision-token budget, compared directly against triple/path-only fine-tuning of the same model.
Same-source-passage (text-aligned) context triples for standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks, most of which use KG-neighborhood retrieval rather than passage-grounded context.
Combining an adaptive one-hop failure detector/repair loop with context-enriched supervision, with one-hop failure rate as a reported diagnostic.
RL optimization restricted to lower-hop instances with an explicit, pre-registered measurement of transfer to deeper hops (hop-depth breakdown and transfer gap).
A relevance-controlled context ablation (same-passage vs shuffled/random triples at fixed budget) to separate 'more tokens' from 'supporting context'.
Separating the value of the answer path from the value of surrounding context at training time (currently only tested at inference time).

contradictions.description: Ordering/merging triplets is claimed to improve answer precision (SG-RAG MOT), whereas a controlled study finds that syntax, triple order, and subgraph size produce no measurable effect at multi-hop depth; only the presence of the answer path matters.

The proposed direction assumes that adding surrounding context triples helps, but the answer-path study finds that replacing all non-chain triples with unrelated-entity material changes multi-hop accuracy by only +0.003 F1, and CLAUSE finds over-retrieval and distractor triples depress accuracy.

Training-free systems are reported competitive with trained systems (Co-E), while trained/embedding-based systems claim state-of-the-art gains (EmbedKGQA, GreaseLM), leaving unclear how much headroom specifically belongs to training-time supervision versus inference-time context.

EmbedKGQA treats KG incompleteness as the central obstacle to multi-hop KGQA, while inference-time context methods largely assume the needed triples can be retrieved or extrapolated at query time; the two framings imply different remedies (link repair vs context construction).
